svg.text: PUSH: how a device sends its local changes to the server
Offline-first restaurant app — Flutter + local SQLite (drift) → Supabase / Postgres. Running example from the staff module: an employee clocks in on a tablet (« Pointage »).

g.text: monospace = table / column names « … » = French UI labels

svg.text: Running example: offline clock-in, then the Wi-Fi comes back
A LOCAL-ONLY SQLite table (outbox), never synced itself. Filled by triggers, emptied by the push.

g.text: the WHOLE row as JSON, as it is NOW

svg.text: UNIQUE INDEX (changed_table, row_key) ⇒ ONE ENTRY PER ROW* busy_dates has no single id: row_key = "store_id|day"
ONE SQLite transaction: row + entry saved together or not at all
Offline banner = live count of outbox rows (callout 5)
À jour — 0 modification en attente (after t5)

g.text: Filled ONLY by SQLite triggers, in the same transaction as the change
AFTER INSERT / AFTER UPDATE on each of the 20 synced tables (change + entry: all or nothing).
No repository writes the outbox by hand. Triggers are generated from the schema: none forgotten.
Merge: a row edited 5× offline keeps ONE entry (upsert)
payload and queued_at are replaced, attempts resets to 0, but the id is KEPT:
a parent created before its children is still sent before them.
Deletes are soft: deleted_at is set (an UPDATE), so the trigger queues it like any edit.
The deletion simply travels inside the payload.
Quiet switch: syncQuiet key in the local meta table
Silences the triggers for writes that must NOT be sent:
rows received from the server, the demo seed, stock recomputation.
Live counter: « N modifications en attente »
The offline banner shows how many outbox rows are waiting.
It reaches 0 once every entry is accepted (or moved to sync_errors).

svg.text: Left = device, right = server. Follow the numbers 1 to 7.
Only ONE pass runs at a time
First, before any row: new photos are uploaded, shrunk to 1024 px JPEG.
SyncRunner reads the first 100 outbox entries, by send order
SELECT … FROM outbox ORDER BY id LIMIT 100
Delete the outbox entry ONLY IF its
Edited during the send? The newer
version stays queued for the next pass.
Moved to the local sync_errors table (table,
rejected_at) and removed: never blocks the queue.
Retry after 5 s → 15 s → 1 min → 5 min
The sync page offers to sign in again:
Loop back to step 1 until the outbox is empty
Max 50 batches per pass. Stop early if a batch made no progress.
Whole batch: is this device registered to the caller's organization?
NO: every entry is rejected and syncing stops (device was removed).
For EACH entry, in its own sub-transaction: one bad entry never blocks the others
Rules checked in this order. The first rule that fails rejects the entry with that reason.

g.text: The table is one of the 20 synced tables
The row's store belongs to the caller's organization
and a stores row may only be written by an owner
A row cannot move to another store
DELETE WINS: a row deleted on the server cannot be edited back
A purchase order's status only moves forward; closed stays closed
A PAID pay period is final (the same retry is still accepted)

svg.text: Otherwise LAST ARRIVAL WINS: insert or replace the whole row, then stamp it
server_seq ← next number of ONE shared global sequence · updated_by_device ← device
store_changes.last_seq ← bumped for that store (used by realtime)
Clients can never write server tables directly: Row Level Security = read-only. Every write goes through push_changes.
The server answers, one result per entry
Example: #41 → accepted, seq 1051 · #42 → accepted, seq 1052 · then outbox empty, banner shows 0
